sourceFile: "25-26-Cycle-of-Prayer.pdf", provided directly by Josh via Google Drive (file id 12IQpC4lm4qxzP154oUlGMoTdsDepTFCy, folder "TEC Cycle of Prayer"); original diocesan source per Josh's own roster: https://episcopalatlanta.org/wp-content/uploads/2025/11/25-26-Cycle-of-Prayer.pdf
notes: The source interleaves fixed-date commemorations/saints' days (e.g. 'Nicholas, Bishop of Myra, c. 342', 'Saint Thomas the Apostle') with no prayer-cycle subject attached to them at all. Only the Sunday-dated cycle rows (bishop attribution + that week's parish/ministry list + the companion-diocese line) are represented in `entries` -- the commemoration-only lines are excluded entirely, not fabricated into empty subject lists.

The source is one continuous cycle, November 30, 2025 through November 29, 2026 (its own title: 'Parish Cycle of Prayer'). Only the 48 weeks landing in calendar 2026 (January 4 through November 29) are in this file, per this corpus's existing cross-liturgical-year convention (see episcopal-alabama-2026.json). The 5 weeks in late 2025 (Nov 30, Dec 7/14/21/28) are deferred to a future episcopal-atlanta-2025.json, not fabricated or force-fit here.

The diocesan bishop's name is printed inconsistently across weeks in the source itself -- 'Bishop Rob Wright' (January 4 and 11 entries only) versus 'Bishop Robert Wright' (every week from January 18 onward) -- preserved exactly as printed per week, not silently normalized to one form.

The companion Diocese of Cape Coast (Church of the Province of West Africa) line -- including any specific companion congregations named that week -- is kept as ONE category subject per week, verbatim, rather than split into separate foreign-parish entries. These are a partner diocese's own congregations in Ghana, not part of the Diocese of Atlanta's own directory the way this schema's 'parish' type is used elsewhere in this corpus.

Several weeks' source text runs a convocation/ministry name directly into the following parish name with no visible separator -- a formatting/line-break loss in the PDF's own text layer, not an error introduced by this transcription (e.g. the source's own run-on 'Marietta Convocation Christ Church, Kennesaw' was split into a 'Mid Atlanta Convocation' category subject and a separate 'Christ Church, Griffin' parish subject once the Easter Sunday entry's own repeated 'The Clergy and people of' phrasing confirmed the boundary). Where a compound phrase's internal structure could not be confidently recovered this way, it was kept as a single verbatim category subject (e.g. 'Ministry of Society of St. Anna the Prophet Church Musicians', February 1) rather than force a guessed split.

Several apparent typos are preserved verbatim per this corpus's standing rule, not silently corrected: 'Ft. Andrew's, Hartwell' (November 29 -- likely 'St. Andrew's'), 'Grace-Calary, Clarkesville' (March 29 -- likely 'Grace-Calvary'), 'St. Luke's, Fort Vally' (October 18 -- likely 'Fort Valley'), and July 5's own liturgical label 'The Fourth Sunday after Pentecost, Proper 9' (numerically inconsistent with the surrounding weekly sequence, which already used 'The Fourth Sunday after Pentecost' for June 21 -- likely should read 'Sixth Sunday').

The diocese's own full published name is not printed anywhere in the source text itself. 'Diocese of Atlanta' is inferred from Bishop Robert Wright's own diocese and the uniformly Georgia place names throughout, not fabricated from nothing, but disclosed here as an inference rather than a directly-quoted title -- unlike the 6 dioceses this corpus ingested first, whose `diocese` field was taken verbatim from each one's own source.

'Cathedral of St. Philip' and 'Cathedral Towers' (May 3 entry) are recorded as category subjects rather than parish subjects because this row of the source names no city for them (this schema's 'parish' type requires an explicit place, and one is not invented here even though the Cathedral's Atlanta location is well known).
